question: Why is my assessment only half of what my house is actually worth? And what limits how much it can go up each year?
notes: CITIZEN VOICE, Proposal A. Const 1963 Art. IX §3 sets uniform ad valorem taxation, assessment at a proportion of true cash value not exceeding 50%, and the taxable-value increase cap. Added 2026-08-03 after the constitution was ingested: §3 retrieved on statutory wording but MISSED on all three citizen phrasings ('half of what my house is worth', 'what limits how much it can go up', 'what is proposal a') — the single most foundational rule in Michigan property tax, invisible to how every taxpayer asks it. This case exists so a synonym regression is caught by the suite rather than by a probe.
